```{python}
import pandas as pd

import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

```

```{python}
data_filtered = pd.read_csv("data_filtered.csv", index_col=0)
```

```{python}
# Map Ensembl IDs to gene symbols 
data_filtered["gene_symbol"] = data_filtered.index.map(genes_metadata["gene_name"])
data_filtered = data_filtered.dropna(subset=["gene_symbol"])
data_filtered = data_filtered.drop_duplicates(subset="gene_symbol", keep="first")
data_filtered = data_filtered.set_index("gene_symbol")
```

```{python}
#ScanB data 
basal_counts = pd.read_csv("counts_scanb_basel.csv", index_col=0)      
sample = pd.read_csv("scanB_clinical_combined.csv",index_col='sample_title')
all_counts= pd.read_csv("scanB_expr_data.csv",index_col=0)
```

```{python}
# log2 CPM from the full filtered counts
cpm_all = data_filtered.div(data_filtered.sum(axis=0), axis=1) * 1e6
logcpm_all = np.log2(cpm_all + 1)
```

### Confounder analysis in ScanB data

```{python}
def zmean(genes, mat):
    g = [x for x in genes if x in mat.index]
    print(f"  {len(g)} of {len(genes)} found: {g}")
    e = mat.loc[g]
    return e.sub(e.mean(axis=1), axis=0).div(e.std(axis=1), axis=0).mean(axis=0)

sets = {
    "ser": ["PHGDH", "PSAT1", "PSPH"],
    "pro": ["MKI67", "TOP2A", "MCM2", "PCNA", "CCNB1", "AURKA", "BIRC5", "CDK1"],
    "hyp": ["CA9", "BNIP3", "NDRG1", "ADM", "VEGFA", "ANKRD37", "EGLN3", "P4HA1", "ERO1A", "BHLHE40"],
    "myc": ["NPM1", "NCL", "CAD", "ODC1", "CCND2", "PPAT", "HSPD1", "EIF4A1"],
    "atf4": ["ASNS", "ATF3", "DDIT3", "TRIB3", "CHAC1", "SLC7A11", "GADD45A"],
}

lab = sample["pam50_subtype"].reindex(all_counts.columns)
ok = lab.isin(["Basal", "LumB"])
ids = ok[ok].index
M = all_counts.loc[:, ids]

d = pd.DataFrame({"basal": (lab[ids] == "Basal").astype(int)})
for k, genes in sets.items():
    print(k + ":")
    d[k] = zmean(genes, M)
    d[k] = (d[k] - d[k].mean()) / d[k].std()

print("\nMedian by group (SD units):")
print(d.groupby("basal")[list(sets)].median().round(2))

# A. Basal vs LumB serine gap, adding covariates one at a time
steps = [("unadjusted", "ser ~ basal"),
         ("+ proliferation", "ser ~ basal + pro"),
         ("+ hypoxia", "ser ~ basal + pro + hyp"),
         ("+ MYC", "ser ~ basal + pro + hyp + myc"),
         ("+ ATF4", "ser ~ basal + pro + hyp + myc + atf4")]
base = None
print("\nSerine gap, Basal vs LumB (SD units):")
for name, f in steps:
    m = smf.ols(f, data=d).fit()
    b = m.params["basal"]; lo, hi = m.conf_int().loc["basal"]
    base = base if base is not None else b
    print(f"  {name:16s} {b:.2f} (95% CI {lo:.2f} to {hi:.2f})  | share kept {b/base:.0%}")

# B. Within Basal: which program tracks serine?
bs = d[d["basal"] == 1].copy()
print("\nWithin Basal (n = %d), Spearman rho with serine:" % len(bs))
for k in ["pro", "hyp", "myc", "atf4"]:
    rho, p = spearmanr(bs[k], bs["ser"])
    print(f"  {k}: rho = {rho:.2f} (p = {p:.2g})")

m = smf.ols("ser ~ pro + hyp + myc + atf4", data=bs).fit()
print("\nJoint model within Basal (standardized coefficients):")
print(pd.DataFrame({"coef": m.params, "p": m.pvalues}).drop("Intercept").round(3))

# C. How collinear are the scores? (values above ~5 mean the joint model is unreliable)
X = bs[["pro", "hyp", "myc", "atf4"]].assign(c=1.0)
vif = {c: variance_inflation_factor(X.values, i) for i, c in enumerate(X.columns) if c != "c"}
print("\nVIF:", {k: round(v, 1) for k, v in vif.items()})
print("Correlations among scores (Basal):")
print(bs[["pro", "hyp", "myc", "atf4"]].corr(method="spearman").round(2))
```

The serine gap survives all four programs, and inside Basal tumors the serine score follows ATF4 and proliferation, not hypoxia. 

Once ATF4 and proliferation are in the model, hypoxia contributes essentially nothing. Earlier, hypoxia looked like a weak driver (coefficient +0.11), but that was without ATF4. This supports your idea that the serine program is not mainly an oxygen-driven response.

The VIFs are all below 2.5, so the four coefficients are separable and the joint model can be read coefficient by coefficient. MYC and proliferation correlate at 0.71, but the VIFs show it isn’t a problem here.

The elevation of serine synthesis genes in Basal-like tumors was only partly explained by proliferation, hypoxia, MYC and ATF4 target expression (77% of the gap retained after adjusting for all four). Within Basal tumors, serine synthesis expression tracked ATF4-target and proliferation scores, and not a hypoxia signature, consistent with a hypoxia-independent, signaling-driven program.

### Testing MRHFD1L

```{python}
def zmean(genes, mat):
    g = [x for x in genes if x in mat.index]
    e = mat.loc[g]
    return e.sub(e.mean(axis=1), axis=0).div(e.std(axis=1), axis=0).mean(axis=0)

sets = {
    "ser": ["PHGDH", "PSAT1", "PSPH"],
    "pro": ["MKI67", "TOP2A", "MCM2", "PCNA", "CCNB1", "AURKA", "BIRC5", "CDK1"],
    "hyp": ["CA9", "BNIP3", "NDRG1", "ADM", "VEGFA", "ANKRD37", "EGLN3", "P4HA1", "BHLHE40"],
    "myc": ["NPM1", "NCL", "CAD", "ODC1", "CCND2", "PPAT", "HSPD1", "EIF4A1"],
    "atf4": ["ASNS", "ATF3", "DDIT3", "TRIB3", "CHAC1", "SLC7A11", "GADD45A"],
}

lab = sample["pam50_subtype"].reindex(all_counts.columns)
ok = lab.isin(["Basal", "LumB"])
ids = ok[ok].index
M = all_counts.loc[:, ids]

mt = pd.DataFrame({"basal": (lab[ids] == "Basal").astype(int)})   # new name, so nothing gets overwritten
for k, genes in sets.items():
    mt[k] = zmean(genes, M)
mt["MTHFD1L"] = M.loc["MTHFD1L"]
for c in list(sets) + ["MTHFD1L"]:
    mt[c] = (mt[c] - mt[c].mean()) / mt[c].std()
print(mt.shape, "| Basal:", mt["basal"].sum(), "| LumB:", (mt["basal"] == 0).sum())   # expect 1127 rows

steps = [("unadjusted", "MTHFD1L ~ basal"),
         ("+ all four programs", "MTHFD1L ~ basal + pro + hyp + myc + atf4"),
         ("+ serine score too", "MTHFD1L ~ basal + pro + hyp + myc + atf4 + ser")]
for name, f in steps:
    m = smf.ols(f, data=mt).fit()
    lo, hi = m.conf_int().loc["basal"]
    print(f"{name:22s} Basal vs LumB: {m.params['basal']:.2f} (95% CI {lo:.2f} to {hi:.2f})")

bs = mt[mt["basal"] == 1]
for k in ["ser", "pro", "atf4", "myc", "hyp"]:
    rho, p = spearmanr(bs["MTHFD1L"], bs[k])
    print(f"Within Basal (n = {len(bs)}): MTHFD1L vs {k}: rho = {rho:.2f} (p = {p:.2g})")
```

MTHFD1L, like the serine synthesis genes, is elevated in Basal-like tumors across cohorts independently of the four programs, while its variation within Basal follows proliferation.

### Confounder analysis replicates in TCGA

```{python}
def zmean(genes, mat):
    g = [x for x in genes if x in mat.index]
    print(f"  {len(g)} of {len(genes)} found" + ("" if len(g) == len(genes) else f": missing {[x for x in genes if x not in g]}"))
    e = mat.loc[g]
    return e.sub(e.mean(axis=1), axis=0).div(e.std(axis=1), axis=0).mean(axis=0)

sets = {
    "ser": ["PHGDH", "PSAT1", "PSPH"],
    "pro": ["MKI67", "TOP2A", "MCM2", "PCNA", "CCNB1", "AURKA", "BIRC5", "CDK1"],
    "hyp": ["CA9", "BNIP3", "NDRG1", "ADM", "VEGFA", "ANKRD37", "EGLN3", "P4HA1", "BHLHE40"],
    "myc": ["NPM1", "NCL", "CAD", "ODC1", "CCND2", "PPAT", "HSPD1", "EIF4A1"],
    "atf4": ["ASNS", "ATF3", "DDIT3", "TRIB3", "CHAC1", "SLC7A11", "GADD45A"],
}

# TCGA tumors only, Basal and LumB (tum = tumor table with BRCA_Subtype_PAM50, indexed by barcode)
t2 = meta_sub [meta_sub ["BRCA_Subtype_PAM50"].isin(["Basal", "LumB"])]
t2 = t2[t2.index.isin(logcpm_all.columns)]
M = logcpm_all.loc[:, t2.index]
print(t2["BRCA_Subtype_PAM50"].value_counts())

d = pd.DataFrame({"basal": (t2["BRCA_Subtype_PAM50"] == "Basal").astype(int)})
for k, genes in sets.items():
    print(k + ":")
    d[k] = zmean(genes, M)
    d[k] = (d[k] - d[k].mean()) / d[k].std()

print("\nMedian by group (SD units):")
print(d.groupby("basal")[list(sets)].median().round(2))

steps = [("unadjusted", "ser ~ basal"),
         ("+ proliferation", "ser ~ basal + pro"),
         ("+ hypoxia", "ser ~ basal + pro + hyp"),
         ("+ MYC", "ser ~ basal + pro + hyp + myc"),
         ("+ ATF4", "ser ~ basal + pro + hyp + myc + atf4")]
base = None
print("\nSerine gap, Basal vs LumB (SD units), TCGA:")
for name, f in steps:
    m = smf.ols(f, data=d).fit()
    b = m.params["basal"]; lo, hi = m.conf_int().loc["basal"]
    base = base if base is not None else b
    print(f"  {name:16s} {b:.2f} (95% CI {lo:.2f} to {hi:.2f})  | share kept {b/base:.0%}")

bs = d[d["basal"] == 1].copy()
print(f"\nWithin Basal (n = {len(bs)}), Spearman rho with serine:")
for k in ["pro", "hyp", "myc", "atf4"]:
    rho, p = spearmanr(bs[k], bs["ser"])
    print(f"  {k}: rho = {rho:.2f} (p = {p:.2g})")

m = smf.ols("ser ~ pro + hyp + myc + atf4", data=bs).fit()
print("\nJoint model within Basal (standardized):")
print(pd.DataFrame({"coef": m.params, "p": m.pvalues}).drop("Intercept").round(3))

X = bs[["pro", "hyp", "myc", "atf4"]].assign(c=1.0)
print("VIF:", {c: round(variance_inflation_factor(X.values, i), 1) for i, c in enumerate(X.columns) if c != "c"})
```

- Roughly four fifths of the serine gap is still there after all four programs are in the model, in both cohorts. The gap is large, and its interval is far from zero.

- Within Basal tumors, ATF4 targets and proliferation are the strongest correlates of the serine score in both cohorts, and the ATF4 coefficient is nearly identical (0.286 and 0.285). Hypoxia contributes little in either one, and its TCGA p-value (0.092) is not significant.

- The VIFs are below 2 here as well, so the coefficients are separable.
